observations: Photo 0: a used longitudinal automatic gearbox with a transfer case bolted to its tail, still attached to a V6 engine, lying on a wet dirty floor among other used engines and gearboxes; dealer watermark 'Gearup Inc' over it.
Photo 0 and photo 2: a white sticker label on the gearbox body near the transfer case, too small and blurred to read; 'CA' and other marks hand-written in chalk or marker on the transfer case.
Photo 0 and photo 2: rust on the output flanges and on a mounting bracket, grime and oil stains on the casing, wiring and cooler lines loose.
Photo 1: the same assembly from the engine side, a V6 with a black plastic intake manifold and yellow dipstick handle, in a yard of other used engines.
No brand, vehicle make or part number is legible on any photo; the Jeep Wrangler fitment comes only from the seller's text.
No photo of the transmission ID tag, the bell housing face, the transfer case shift lever or the inside of the pan.

identity.kind: used 4x4 automatic gearbox with transfer case (shown attached to a V6 engine)
read_from: photo 0 and photo 2 gearbox and transfer case shape

claims.claim: Gearbox / transmission for Jeep Wrangler 3.6L 2011 to 2017 4x4
claims.evidence: Photos 0 to 2 show a longitudinal automatic with transfer case behind a V6, which fits the claim, but no Jeep marking or part number is readable; the label in photos 0 and 2 is blurred.

claims.claim: Direct America (foreign used, imported from the US)
claims.evidence: Origin cannot be seen; no import papers or donor vehicle shown.
Text is cut off and no odometer photo of the donor vehicle is shown.
Photos 0 and 2 show rusted flanges and bracket, grime and oil staining, and the unit lying on a wet yard floor among scrap parts: it is a used pulled unit.
Internal history cannot be seen; pan and bolt heads are not shown up close.
No clip of it running in a vehicle or on a test bench.
No receipt or warranty card is shown, and the item is a used pulled part.

risks.risk: Gearbox is not the Wrangler 3.6 unit (wrong model, wrong year range or 2WD variant), which sets the price and whether it fits at all.
risks.proof: Sharp close-up of the white ID label on the gearbox showing the part number, plus a photo of the transfer case tag.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced as a Wrangler gearbox; held until the tag is read

risks.risk: Internal wear: slipping, harsh shifts, burnt clutches or a failed valve body or TCM.
risks.proof: Clip of the gearbox in a running vehicle or test rig going through every gear, plus a photo of the fluid on the dipstick or drain plug.

risks.risk: Transfer case faulty or missing its shift motor or lever.
risks.proof: Clip shifting the transfer case through 2H, 4H, N and 4L and a photo of its tag.
risks.if_unproven: priced as gearbox only, transfer case as scrap

risks.risk: It is unclear whether the engine shown attached is part of the sale.
risks.proof: Seller's written confirmation and a photo of exactly the parts included, laid out separately.

risks.risk: Cracked casing or damaged bell housing or mounting ears.
risks.proof: Clear photos of the bell housing face and all sides of the casing once separated from the engine.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the worst seen condition

proof_requests: Sharp close-up of the gearbox ID label showing the part number
Photo of the transfer case tag
Clip of the gearbox shifting through every gear in a running vehicle or on a test rig
Photo of the fluid colour and the drain plug magnet
Photo of exactly what is included, engine attached or not
response.reason: No make, model or part number can be read in any photo, and the fitment that sets the price comes only from the seller's text, so not even a worst case price is possible until the ID label is shown; the 'like new' claim is contradicted by the visibly used, rusted unit.
